cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: Engineering drawings communicate design intent precisely using standardised conventions and symbols.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: Orthographic projection shows multiple 2D views: front elevation, plan and side elevation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: Third angle projection places views in the orientation seen from that direction (the UK standard).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: Isometric drawing shows a 3D view at 30 degrees with no perspective distortion; all axes at true scale.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: Section views show internal features by cutting through the component; hatching indicates cut material.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: Assembly drawings show how components fit together, with a parts list and item numbers.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: Dimensioning rules: dimensions must be clear, not duplicated, and placed to show functional relationships.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: Tolerances specify acceptable variation using +/- values or limit dimensions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: Surface finish symbols indicate required smoothness (Ra value in micrometres).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: CAD creates 3D models and 2D drawings using software such as SolidWorks or Fusion 360.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: CAM converts CAD data into machine instructions (G-code) for CNC machines.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM
cards.back: CAD/CAM integration: the 3D model generates toolpaths automatically, linking design to production.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — engineering drawings & cad/cam?
cards.back: 1. For Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Engineering Drawings & CAD/CAM through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant
An engineer needs to communicate a bracket design with an internal bore and two mounting holes to a manufacturer. Describe the drawing package required. [6 marks]

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of engineering drawings & cad/cam, including materials, manufacturing processes and engineering systems relevant to AQA 8852 & WJEC Eduqas 5799QA. AO2 (Application): Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering drawings & cad/cam to analyse, design and manufacture engineering solutions. AO3 (Evaluation): Evaluate engineer
